case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: The instruction and visible start state appear to ask the agent to record every trip-expense note in Simple Note into the already created corresponding Splitwise group: Cairo, Seoul, Venice, Tokyo, and Santorini.
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: The released evaluator loads this task's private_data and only accepts added Expense and ExpenseShare mappings for groups 274, 275, and 276. Tokyo 277 and Santorini 278 are omitted from the target, so records that add those visible trip expenses fail tests 3-7 and therefore fail because TestTracker.success is pass_count == num_tests.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: Confirmed target-construction defect. The start state exposes five matching expense notes and five matching trip groups, but private_data only encodes Cairo, Seoul, and Venice. That omission changes the checked outcome.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: The evaluator logic itself is internally consistent: it registers only the ten `with test(...)` checks and compares the run against the narrowed private_data target. `test.task_completed` is an unscored dynamic attribute, so there is no separate evaluator-registration bug beyond the incomplete target.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: No separate reward-wiring or aggregation defect was found. The official worker serializes the TestTracker, released success is tracker.success, and Metric only aggregates after the per-record tracker is already fixed.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: The official case appears to claim that all visible trip notes with corresponding Splitwise groups should be recorded, but the released target only scores three of the five matching trips. Records that also post the visible Tokyo and Santorini expenses are failed for doing so.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: The frozen checklist and case packet preserve the official native semantics: the ten registered tests, their conjunction, and the separation between native and stronger conditions. I found no checklist or case-packet misstatement of official native evaluator behavior.

records.different_outcome_description: The apparent task outcome was to record all five visible trip-expense notes into their corresponding existing Splitwise groups, including Tokyo 277 and Santorini 278. This record did post those Tokyo and Santorini expenses, but the released evaluator failed it because private_data only targets Cairo, Seoul, and Venice and therefore treats groups 277 and 278 as wrong extra additions.
records.reason: This record is bound to task 32616b5_1 on test_normal under the pinned official runtime, and its retained API and DB artifacts show Tokyo and Santorini expenses were created exactly in the corresponding visible groups. The native evaluator output shows the record failed only the mapping tests that compare against the narrowed three-group private_data target. That is a different checked outcome, not merely a weaker operationalization of the same outcome.

issues.description: `score.json` marked `bind_expense_descriptions_to_source_rows` as supported even though the frozen stronger condition is scoped to corresponding applicable source-note rows, and the scorer-visible evidence shows extra Tokyo and Santorini expenses in groups 277 and 278 with no corresponding applicable rows under that frozen scope. The stronger verdict should therefore be `F`, not `S`.
